## ADR-0149 — `demos/traces/**` is regenerated by the build and freshness-diffed by CI; and two standing rules finally reach the rulings register

**Status:** Accepted (author-directed, autonomous session per R30),
2026-08-17.

### Context

`demos/traces/**` was the last ungated derived-artifact tree in the
repo. ADR-0142 established that negatively and carefully — no `Makefile`
target, no workflow, no test referenced the path, across all seventeen
targets and `docsgen`'s seven dependencies; the only tracked mechanism
touching it at all was `.gitattributes:27`'s `-text`, which protects the
bytes from EOL rewriting and checks nothing about whether they are
current.

That session also showed what the gap costs. Regenerating three
strip-bearing files by hand, it found `order-result/messages.txt` had
been captured *before* PV1 gained its trailing positional fields and had
sat wrong through an entire milestone, while `emit-state/README.md`'s
claim that the two files were "the same" was simply false. ADR-0142 fixed
the bytes, wrote a dated errata, and registered the missing gate as
`roadmap.md#demos-traces-ungated` rather than building it.

The row was scheduled ahead of `#event-log-shape-defects` (PRIORITY 1)
for a specific reason: the S-row and Z-segment work there *moves these
traces*, and today nothing would notice.

This session builds the gate. It also carries a rider: two standing rules
that have been governing sessions from prompt preambles and ADR addenda
while `.agents/rulings.md` — the register that exists so a cold session
can find "what rule applies going forward" — still stated the rule one of
them replaced.

### Step 0 — baseline, and a census that went differently than predicted

`bin/preflight` findings, all disclosed before proceeding: a RED run
(`77f4fba8`) among the last five on `main`, which is the red half of
ADR-0147's own `R-red-pushed-with-green` pair and red by construction;
tree clean including untracked; edit root on ext4, not `/mnt/*`; HEAD ==
`origin/main` at `922e55a`; last tag
`stable-20260817-exercised-sources-coverage` at `854a0df`, HEAD untagged
and no tag owed.

Baseline `make test`, unpiped, `MAKE_EXIT=0`, 14m52s: **344 blocks,
3,906 tests, 17,548 assertions**, zero failures and zero errors —
reconciling *exactly* with ADR-0148's recorded counts. `poly check`
green, `verify-nist-lock` green.

#### Two findings the census turned up before it ran

**Five of six `ground-truth.edn` carry CRLF in this working tree and LF
in HEAD.** `.gitattributes:1` is `* text=auto eol=lf`, so git normalizes
on comparison and `git status` stays silent about it. Every byte
comparison in this ADR is therefore against `git show HEAD:<path>`, never
the worktree copy — `wc -c` on the checkout is off by one per line for
those files. (`messages*.txt` are `-text`, so worktree and HEAD agree
byte-for-byte there; verified, all seven.) A side effect of this session:
`make traces` rewrote them as LF, so the clone now agrees with HEAD.

**The seven `messages*.txt` end in three different byte shapes.** Three
files end with a bare `\r` and no trailing newline (emit-state,
order-result, persona-enriched); two end `\r\r\n` (boarding-transfer,
module-mix); two end `\r\n\n` (both site-profiles). `main!` prints
bare-text through `println`, so *at most one* of those three shapes can
be a faithful `--format er7` capture. Before any content question was
asked, the tree had already recorded that these files were captured by
three different methods.

#### Prediction, recorded before running

Written to the scratchpad before the first command: **persona-enriched
diverges** (its own README says so at :27-30); **the other six are
byte-identical**, having been regenerated at ADR-0142 or predicted frozen
by that ADR's own trace-movers table.

#### Actual

Each README's own `--emit hl7` command, run with `--format er7` (7 runs,
7.2–8.4 s wall each, under load from the baseline suite):

| file | HEAD | fresh | class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `boarding-transfer/messages.txt` | 21,560 | 21,559 | mechanical — one stray `\r` before EOF; content identical to byte 21,558 |
| `emit-state/messages.txt` | 5,822 | 5,823 | mechanical — the committed file is missing the trailing newline; first 5,822 bytes identical |
| `module-mix/messages.txt` | 19,637 | 16,851 | **other** — see below |
| `order-result/messages.txt` | 5,822 | 5,823 | mechanical — same missing newline |
| `persona-enriched/messages.txt` | 2,905 | 3,206 | ADR-0142-disclosed — PV1 trailing positional fields, PV1-36 on discharges, nothing else |
| `site-profiles/messages-default.txt` | 1,293 | 1,292 | mechanical — a doubled trailing newline |
| `site-profiles/messages-aldric.txt` | 1,538 | 1,537 | mechanical — a doubled trailing newline |

**Prediction vs actual: wrong on six of seven, right on the one that
mattered least.** Only persona-enriched was called correctly. The honest
reading is that the prediction was about *content* and was right about
content in five of the six misses — but it was stated as byte identity,
and byte identity is what a freshness gate enforces. No two of the seven
files were captured the same way, and a prediction drawn from ADR-0142's
content-level movers table could not have seen that. The lesson belongs
to the prediction, not to the tree: **an ungated artifact drifts in
capture *method* as readily as in content, and only the method drift is
invisible to a content-level census.**

#### The one "other", and why it did not become a STOP

`module-mix/messages.txt` was not close: 70 messages committed against 60
fresh, different MRNs, different dates, different patients. Not PV1, not
OBR-7/OBX-14, not whitespace. The fence makes an "other" a STOP, and this
one also looked like the textbook two-defensible-readings case — a stale
trace, or engine drift that committing today's bytes would launder into
the record.

Probed rather than reported. Two runs settled it:

1. **Determinism** — a second fresh run is byte-identical to the first,
   so the fresh side is not noise.
2. **The era probe** — a disposable worktree at `f07684c`, *the commit
   that last wrote this file*, running that README's own command,
   produces **16,851 bytes, byte-identical to today's fresh output**.

So the engine has not moved this trace at all, in a hundred-odd commits.
The committed bytes were never the output of the command the README
teaches — not today, and not in the commit that landed them. The "engine
drift" reading is not merely less likely; it is refuted. One defensible
reading survives, which makes this fix-forward-with-disclosure and not a
STOP — F-3 narrowed, the rule this session lands as
`rulings.md#R-stop-only-on-two-defensible-readings` an hour later.

That is also the sharpest single argument for this session's existence.
ADR-0142 found a trace stale by one milestone. This one found a trace
that was *never right*, and neither could have been found by reading.

#### `ground-truth.edn`, and the pprint question answered without tuning

The CLI's `--format ground-truth` is `pr-str` — one line, readable
straight back by `edn/read` (that is its job; it feeds `ehrt sim check`),
and not what is committed. Piping it through `clojure.pprint/pprint` **at
its default margin, with no configuration of any kind**:

| file | HEAD | pprint | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `boarding-transfer/ground-truth.edn` | 31,981 | 31,981 | **identical** |
| `emit-state/ground-truth.edn` | 8,785 | 8,785 | **identical** |
| `module-mix/ground-truth.edn` | 319,714 | 318,661 | differs (the same wrong capture) |
| `order-result/ground-truth.edn` | 8,785 | 8,785 | **identical** |
| `persona-enriched/ground-truth.edn` | 5,159 | 5,159 | **identical** |
| `site-profiles/ground-truth.edn` | 2,067 | 2,067 | **identical** |

Five of six, byte-for-byte, first try. Worth noticing that
persona-enriched's ground truth is identical *while its messages
diverge by 301 bytes* — PV1 is a rendering surface, not a ground-truth
fact, and the emitter-coherence law shows up here as a census result
rather than as an assertion.

#### The FHIR bundle

`emit-state/fhir-bundle-patient1.json` is patient 1's bundle out of the
`--emit fhir` envelope's `{patient-id -> Bundle}` map, pretty-printed by
`clojure.data.json/pprint`. Fresh output differs from HEAD by **five
bytes on one line**: the committed file wraps `"identifier":` onto its
own line, the default margin does not.

Probed for the exact cause: `*print-right-margin*` **71** reproduces the
committed file byte-for-byte; the default 72 produces the one re-wrap.
The prompt's criterion is "byte-for-byte **or in mechanical-only
variance**", and a single line re-wrap is squarely the latter, so the
bundle is regenerated rather than left as residue.

**Pinning 71 was rejected deliberately.** It would buy a zero-byte diff
with a magic number no future reader could justify, and would leave one
namespace printing EDN at one margin and JSON at another. The default is
used for both surfaces, and the one re-wrapped line is disclosed here.

### The marker/row decision, and the evidence for it

The prompt asked whether six `:source` rows can key to ONE `:script` with
distinct marker pairs, or whether the register assumes one script per
source and six scripts are needed.

**One script, six marker pairs, six rows.** The evidence, probed before
choosing:

- `strip-fresh/check-entry` takes `:marker-open`/`:marker-close` from the
  row and passes them through to `demo-exerciser-fresh/check` — the
  ADR-0130 widening exists precisely so a marker pair is row data rather
  than a namespace literal.
- `exercised-sources-coverage-test`'s `row-id` is `source " -> " script`.
  Six rows sharing a script stay distinct because their sources differ.
- `:section` disambiguates a **source** with several rows (README.md's
  own two), which none of these is. Nothing anywhere keys on script
  uniqueness.
- `bin/regen-traces` is not exerciser-shaped under
  `exercised-sources-coverage-test`'s own naming convention
  (`usecase-` prefix or `exerciser` infix), so no gate *forced* these
  rows. They are here because the tree-population closure this session
  adds requires them, not because a test demanded them.

Six scripts would have been six copies of one apparatus, and `make
traces` would still have had to invoke all six. The widening uses the
register's existing shape; it does not change it.

The one real cost is disclosed in `exercised_sources_test.clj`'s own
docstring: `registry-seeds-the-five-new-rows-test` builds a `by-script`
map, which now collapses the six new rows onto one key. That test only
looks up the older, unique scripts, so it stays honest — but a future
assertion keyed on `:script` alone would not be, and the file now says so.

### What landed

`bin/regen-traces` runs each of the six trace READMEs' fenced commands
verbatim, between per-trace `BEGIN`/`END` markers, under `expect`
exit-code assertions, and materializes all fifteen derived files through
**one** JVM (`ehrt.docs-tooling.trace-capture`). `make traces` is a new
`docsgen` leaf; CI's freshness step diffs `demos/traces/`.

Two deliberate deviations from `bin/demo-exerciser-ed-tuesday`, whose
shape it otherwise reuses verbatim:

1. `expect` does not echo captured stdout. ed-tuesday echoes so a human
   sees normal output; here a single step's stdout runs to ~300 KB of EDN
   and `make traces` would bury its own result. Byte counts are printed
   instead.
2. **Two runs are apparatus**, outside any marker block and invisible to
   the freshness check. boarding-transfer's and module-mix's READMEs
   teach only a `--format er7` command, which renders messages and no
   ground truth, so their `ground-truth.edn` has no taught command that
   yields it. Each apparatus run is the taught command *minus* `--format
   er7`, and the script then proves it is the same run by rebuilding the
   ER7 bytes from its envelope and `cmp`ing them against the taught
   command's own captured stdout. An apparatus run that had drifted from
   its taught sibling fails loudly rather than quietly writing a ground
   truth from different traffic.

Three claims that were prose are now checked on every regeneration:

- the two apparatus envelopes rebuild their taught `--format er7` bytes
  exactly (which also re-proves `sim-er7-bare-text`'s join rule against
  real captured output, every time);
- site-profiles' two profiles share one byte-identical ground truth —
  that README's own invariance thesis, and the reason ONE
  `ground-truth.edn` is committed there rather than two;
- emit-state and order-result render byte-identical messages — the exact
  claim ADR-0142 found already drifted once.

`ehrt.docs-tooling.traces-fresh-test` holds four claims, all red at
`922e55a` (19 failures, 0 errors): population closure over the tree; the
pinned taught-command count per README on *both* sides; `docsgen` depends
on `traces` and `traces` runs `bin/regen-traces`; and CI's diff list
names `demos/traces/`.

**Premise corrected, disclosed.** The prompt placed the population
assertion in `docsgen_test`, "how the population is derived so the new
paths join it, not a hand list." It is derived nowhere. `docsgen_test`
covers `render-cli-md` and nothing else, and ADR-0136's widening of the
CI diff list from five paths to ten was recorded as a *comment* in the
workflow — "if a new derived file appears, it goes on a make target AND
on the diff list below, same commit" — with no gate behind it. Claims (c)
and (d) are the first mechanical check of either surface. The sentence
ADR-0136 wrote is now enforced rather than remembered.

### Read-back, per regenerated file

Nine files changed. Sizes are HEAD bytes before, committed bytes after.

| file | before | after | Δ | change class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `boarding-transfer/messages.txt` | 21,560 | 21,559 | −1 | mechanical |
| `emit-state/messages.txt` | 5,822 | 5,823 | +1 | mechanical |
| `emit-state/fhir-bundle-patient1.json` | 6,073 | 6,068 | −5 | mechanical |
| `module-mix/messages.txt` | 19,637 | 16,851 | −2,786 | never its own command's output |
| `module-mix/ground-truth.edn` | 319,714 | 318,661 | −1,053 | never its own command's output |
| `order-result/messages.txt` | 5,822 | 5,823 | +1 | mechanical |
| `persona-enriched/messages.txt` | 2,905 | 3,206 | +301 | ADR-0142-disclosed (PV1) |
| `site-profiles/messages-default.txt` | 1,293 | 1,292 | −1 | mechanical |
| `site-profiles/messages-aldric.txt` | 1,538 | 1,537 | −1 | mechanical |

Four `ground-truth.edn` (boarding-transfer, emit-state, order-result,
persona-enriched) regenerate **byte-identical to HEAD** — same blob hash;
`git status` lists them only on the stat cache, because their worktree
CRLF was replaced by the LF that HEAD already carried.

**No "other" survives.** module-mix's class was resolved by the
`f07684c` probe to a single defensible reading before its bytes were
committed.

Three READMEs carry a dated errata line, each where this change makes the
page's own words false: persona-enriched's staleness note ("not a
byte-for-byte match ... today"), emit-state's "byte-identical at 5,822
bytes" and its "nothing in the build regenerates or freshness-checks"
clause, and order-result's "no `Makefile` target, no CI job, no test".
This is the fence's own carve-out applied three times rather than once;
leaving a README asserting a false byte count would have been the worse
reading of "no prose edits".

### Timings, and the tier question left open

| measurement | wall |
|---|---|
| `make traces`, cold `out/` | **83.65 s** |
| `make docsgen` (twelve leaves) | 119.40 s |
| `make docsgen` before this session | ~36 s |
| a second `make traces` (idempotence) | 15 files, sha256-equal, no diff |

**83.65 s against the prompt's 90 s ceiling, so no STOP fired and no
per-push-vs-integration tier ruling is forced.** The margin is thin and
is recorded rather than glossed: `traces` is now by far the slowest
`docsgen` leaf — eleven `bin/ehrt` starts (~7.3 s each, almost all of it
JVM and classpath) plus one materializing JVM — and CI pays it on every
push. Two of the eleven are the apparatus runs; two more are the
identical `--emit hl7` command taught by both `order-result` and
`emit-state`, which must appear in both marker blocks and therefore runs
twice. A future session wanting the number down should look there first,
and at the fact that a single JVM could do all eleven if the freshness
contract did not require the taught commands to run as taught.

### The rider: two standing rules reach the register

`rulings.md#R-law-surface-propagation` (ADR-0055) says an amendment to
standing law lands on every surface stating that law, in the session that
rules it. Two rules had missed that.

Grepped before adding, per the prompt: neither was captured under another
slug. `.agents/rulings.md` held four `STOP-AND-REPORT` mentions, none
about this condition, and no row mentioning `gh` at all.

- **`R-unrelayed-tag-condition-stops`** keeps its row and gains
  `SUPERSEDED-BY R-session-verifies-ci-via-gh (ADR-0148)`. Nothing is
  deleted; ADR-0134's reasoning still explains why the old rule existed
  and why the trust boundary moved.
- **`R-session-verifies-ci-via-gh`** (ADR-0148) — sources:
  `notes/adr/0147-compression-arc-close.md:180` and `:420` ("conclusion
  **`success`**, read with `gh run view` before tagging"), ADR-0148's own
  addendum (run `32078358238` at `854a0df`, both branches of the
  two-branch licence written out), and the standing line carried
  identically in the last four archived session prompts.
- **`R-stop-only-on-two-defensible-readings`** (ADR-0146) — sources:
  `notes/adr/0146-emitter-author-ux.md:370` (U-14: "Mechanical, one
  defensible reading, so it fixes forward with this disclosure rather
  than stopping (F-3 narrowed)"), and ADR-0148 at `:64` and `:255`.

The second of those got its first use in this session an hour before it
was written down, on module-mix.

### The session's own red, and what it says about verification

CI at `76b4e20` concluded `failure` on one assertion:
`ehrt.cli.executable-bits-test` found `bin/regen-traces` at mode `100644`
in the index. This clone runs `core.fileMode=false`, so `chmod +x` made
the worktree file executable and `git add` recorded `100644` anyway --
exactly the mismatch that gate reads the index rather than the working
tree in order to see.

It is worth recording why it reached CI. The Step 2 verification ran
`clojure -M:poly test brick:docs-tooling`, on the reasoning that the
change was confined to docs-tooling, `bin/`, the `Makefile` and the
workflow. That reasoning was wrong in a specific way: the *change* was
confined, but a gate that scans the whole tree lives in another brick,
and a tree-scanning gate is answerable to every commit regardless of
where the diff falls. **A targeted brick run is not a substitute for the
full suite before a push, however narrow the change looks** -- and it is
the second instance of this class in two weeks (`bin/state-migrate-0147`,
ADR-0147 S-7).

Fixed forward with disclosure -- one defensible reading, so no STOP,
which is this session's third application of the rule it landed:
`git update-index --chmod=+x bin/regen-traces`, then a sweep of every
tracked file under `bin/` and `.githooks/` confirming it was the only
offender (`rulings.md#R-population-closure`).

Because `poly test` failed, CI **skipped** the generated-doc freshness
step -- so the `demos/traces/` diff this session added to that step had
not run anywhere. Rather than push and find out, the CI condition was
reproduced locally on a real `git clone --no-local` of the pushed tip:

- **Before the fix**, `make traces` in the fresh clone died at
  `execvp: bin/regen-traces: Permission denied`, exit 127. The bit was
  not merely a lint failure -- it would have broken the freshness step
  itself. A stronger witness than the assertion that caught it.
- **After the fix**, `make traces` exits 0 and `git diff --exit-code
  demos/traces/` exits 0. **The committed bytes regenerate exactly from
  a fresh checkout**, which is the whole claim this session makes.

That also settles the line-ending question end to end: a fresh clone gets
LF `ground-truth.edn` and byte-verbatim `-text` `messages*.txt`, and
`make traces` writes exactly those bytes back.

One residual risk remains named rather than claimed closed: the fresh
clone ran on this machine's JVM. Whether a *different* JVM produces the
same map iteration order in the pretty-printed EDN and JSON is something
only CI can answer, and the freshness gate is precisely the instrument
that would report it if not.

### Residue

None. Every derived file under `demos/traces/**` — seven
`messages*.txt`, six `ground-truth.edn`, one FHIR bundle — is regenerated
by `make traces` and diffed by CI. The FHIR bundle was the one candidate
for a residue row and went in on the mechanical-variance branch instead,
so `roadmap.md#demos-traces-ungated` closes without one.

What is *not* closed, and is not this session's business: the
`module-mix` trace is now correct, but nobody has asked what its
committed bytes were a capture *of*. They were internally consistent HL7
at a different seed or config, so they came from somewhere. The question
is archaeology, the file is right now, and the gate makes it stay right.
Named here rather than registered, since there is nothing to act on.
